tools.name: accessiBe
tools.entry_price_terms: Micro · per month for up to 5,000 monthly visits
tools.price_note: (2026-09-10, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers for accessWidget, priced per monthly website visits, with both a monthly and a yearly rate on every tier: Micro $59/month or $490/year up to 5,000 visits a month, Growth $179/month or $1,490/year up to 30,000, Scale $479/month or $3,990/year up to 100,000, and Enterprise on quote above that. Micro covers automated scans and fixes every 24 hours, an accessibility statement and report, and email plus live chat. Growth adds a dedicated case manager, Google Analytics integration, multi-account and team management, and a two-day response target. Scale adds one hour with an ADA attorney, a yearly round of manual testing and validation by their experts, and custom fixes. Enterprise adds 5 to 10 attorney hours, on-demand testing, SSO and a dedicated account manager. The page opens on the yearly toggle, so $490 is the first figure a visitor sees; switching it to 'Billed monthly' shows the monthly rates above. Paying yearly saves about 30% against twelve monthly payments, which is what the toggle's own SAVE 30% label claims. No free plan and no trial is listed.

tools.name: AccuWeb Hosting
tools.entry_price_terms: VPS Edge · per month on a 24-month term, New York location
tools.price_note: (read 2026-10-07 on accuwebhosting.com/pricing/vps-hosting in a browser render from a Netherlands connection, which showed euros, with the 24-month term and the New York location selected) Four Linux VPS plans. VPS Edge is €4.42 a month and renews at €8.91: 4 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 50 GB storage, 250 GB bandwidth, 1 IP. VPS Peak, marked Most Popular, is €6.20 and renews at €17.83: 8 GB RAM, 2 vCPU, 100 GB, 450 GB bandwidth. VPS Power is €8.88 and renews at €35.68: 16 GB RAM, 3 vCPU, 200 GB, 650 GB bandwidth. VPS Supreme is €17.80 and renews at €71.36: 32 GB RAM, 4 vCPU, 400 GB, 1,000 GB bandwidth. The page advertises savings of 69% to 84% on these introductory prices, a 7-day money-back guarantee, 24/7 support and a 99.9% uptime guarantee. The home page, in US dollars, lists VPS hosting from $4.95 a month, Windows VPS from $6.33, Enterprise WordPress Cloud from $6.99, and dedicated servers from $103.00 a month in the USA and $149.00 in Frankfurt or Singapore, with a 99.99% uptime SLA on dedicated servers.

tools.name: ADP
tools.price_note: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, and we checked four places before saying so. /pricing returns a 404, and so does /pricing.md. The RUN product page offers only a “Get Pricing” button. And the dedicated package-comparison page lists all four tiers with “Get pricing” under each one and not a single figure. The tiers are Essential Payroll, Enhanced Payroll (adds ZipRecruiter, State Unemployment Insurance and garnishment payments), Complete Payroll & HR Plus (adds basic HR support) and HR Pro Payroll & HR (enhanced HR support and staff perks). A promotion was running when we read it: three months of free payroll, marked “Ends 8/27”, with terms behind an asterisk. Re-checked 11 October 2026 in a live browser: the package-comparison page still shows Get pricing under all four tiers and no figure. The banner now reads 'Get 3 months FREE when you sign up for small business payroll. Ends 10/22.' Its terms (adp.com/terms/3-month-offer-terms.aspx) say the sales order must be signed and payroll started by October 22, 2026, processing must continue for three consecutive months at the original bundle, pay frequency and discount level, fees must be paid by direct debit, and the free months are credited to months 4, 5 and 6, not the first three. The offer is for new RUN clients with 1-49 employees in the continental U.S.; non-payroll services, pass-through costs, delivery and off-cycle fees are excluded.

flags.evidence: No published price: pricing page and package page return only "Get Pricing" buttons, no figure anywhere (read 15 Aug 2026)

tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-10) Quote-only. Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250. That page is gone — both airia.com/pricing and www.airia.com/pricing now redirect to airia.ai/docs/build/interface-options/usage_limits, a developer documentation page titled Usage Limits on a different domain, while airia.ai/pricing answered 200 with an empty shell on 10 September and on 10 October 2026 redirects to the Airia sign-in page. Treat any $50 or $250 figure still in circulation, including in older versions of this review, as historical rather than current.

tools.name: Airwallex
tools.entry_price_terms: a month per active Spend user plus a team-size platform fee
tools.price_note: (2026-08-28, read off their own pricing page and fee table; re-read 2026-10-11 on airwallex.com/en-us/pricing: plans, FX, transfer, card and billing rates unchanged; re-read 2026-10-23 on the same page: plans and rates again unchanged, with a 0.4% per-transaction fee for automatic tax calculation in the billing table that our earlier readings did not record, and restamped Yield figures) FX conversion 0.5% above the interbank rate for major currencies and 1% for all others. Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. Payment acceptance 2.8% + $0.30 on domestic cards and 4.30% + $0.30 on international cards; local payment methods $0.30 plus method-specific fees. Corporate cards carry no international fees and up to 2% cash rebate on local USD spend. Account plans: Explore free, Grow $12 per active Spend user/month plus a platform fee that varies with team size, Accelerate custom. Their table adds limits the earlier reading did not record: the first 10 Spend users are free and the $12 rate runs to 250 Spend users; the monthly fee is charged per business legal entity, with up to 3 entities included; for each additional entity the footnote now says only that additional fees may apply (our 28 August reading recorded $1,000); subscription and usage-based billing cost 0.50% per successful transaction while invoicing is free; and USD balances earn a Yield rate that Airwallex restamps daily rather than fixing per plan — on 23 October 2026 the US page showed 3.44% on Explore, 3.59% on Grow and 3.71% on Accelerate (3.42%, 3.57% and 3.69% on 11 October), and its own footnote reads that the indicative rate is the 7-day annualized historical rate of the underlying funds as of October 22, 2026, net of fees. Read those three figures as a moving number carrying the date the page gave it, not as a plan feature: they were 3.21%, 3.36% and 3.48% when we first recorded them on 28 August and 3.22%, 3.37% and 3.49% on 5 and 19 September.

tools.name: Alohi
tools.entry_price_terms: a month billed annually ($83.99/yr)
tools.price_note: (read 2026-09-10 and re-read unchanged 2026-09-27 on fax.plus/pricing and sign.plus/pricing) Priced per product, in USD, with a currency switcher offering EUR, CHF and GBP. IMPORTANT: on Fax.Plus the '/month' figure on each card is the annual rate. Fax.Plus — Basic $6.99 a month billed as $83.99 annually (200 pages a month, one fax number, one member, $0.10 per extra page, 60 pages maximum per fax); Premium $13.99 / $167.99 (500 pages, $0.07 per extra page, 90 pages per fax, adds toll-free numbers, number porting, CSV log export and the ability to switch off reception); Business $27.99 / $335.99 (1,000 pages); Enterprise $79.99 a month on annual billing, $959.99 a year, and the only card that also shows a monthly-billing rate, 'starts at $99.99' (4,000 pages, multiple fax numbers, unlimited members, $0.03 per extra page, 250 pages per fax, 1,000 AI credits a month, SSO, HIPAA-compliant with BAA, the Fax.Plus API, data residency and Zapier). The banner offers 'up to 3 months free with an annual plan (save up to 22%)'. A free plan gives 10 pages in total, not per month. Extra fax numbers are $4.99 a month (Business and Enterprise include two); vanity numbers $19.99; choosing your own number within a region is a one-time $19.99, or $29.99 from their handpicked memorable set. Porting is free but country-dependent — porting a US or Canadian number requires Premium or higher. The footnotes warn that faxes to certain destinations may count as multiple pages, priced on a separate Sending Rates page, and that taxes are excluded. Sign.Plus is a separate subscription and prints annual and monthly rates side by side: Free (3 signature requests in total, 1 template, 1 user), Personal $9.99 annual / $14.99 monthly, $119.99 a year (1 user, 10 signature requests a month, 5 templates), Professional $19.99 / $29.99 per user, $239.99 a year (up to 5 users, unlimited requests, 10 templates), Business $29.99 / $49.99 per user, $359.99 a year (unlimited templates, document sharing, Zapier, custom branding), Enterprise $49.99 / $79.99 per user, $599.99 a year (SSO, HIPAA-compliant with BAA, advanced security controls, data residency, priority support). Sign.Plus advertises 'save up to 40% with annual plans'. Request via SMS/WhatsApp is metered separately at 10, 30 and 150 a month from Professional upward. The Fax.Plus page's structured product data, read 27 September 2026, also lists monthly-billing prices for the lower tiers that the cards do not print: Basic $8.99, Premium $17.99, Business $34.99 and Enterprise $99.99 a month.

tools.name: Alvys
tools.price_note: (re-verified 20 Sep 2026) The pricing page is public again, and it has tiers now. On 26 August 2026 alvys.com/pricing answered an ordinary request with HTTP 401 and sat behind a password; read on 20 September 2026 it returns 200 and shows three plans — Foundations, Growth and Scale — none of which carries an amount. All three read "Quoted based on volume of loads", under the page's own summary line: simple per-load pricing, free implementation, cancel anytime. Foundations now has a 14-day free trial behind a Try for free button; Growth and Scale route to sales. The FAQ states there are no setup fees, no per-user or per-seat charge, no contracts and month-to-month cancellation. Two extras are priced in the open: EDI includes 2 trading partners on Growth and 5 on Scale with per-partner pricing above the cap, and the developer sandbox is a $100/month add-on on Foundations and Growth, included on Scale. Custom reports, scheduled reports, Insights AI analytics, Sage and Samsara Premium are add-ons on every tier. The last published load-based rates (2026) were Carrier from ~$150/mo and Broker from ~$300/mo; those tier names no longer exist on the page and the figures are history, not a quote.

tools.name: Aplos
tools.entry_price_terms: Lite · billed monthly, as published for all three tiers
tools.price_note: (2026-10-13, read on their own pricing page and in their help centre) Three published tiers, billed monthly: Lite at $79/month, Core at $129 and Advanced at $229, plus a fourth Custom tier with tailored pricing aimed at organisations above $1 million in annual revenue. Advanced is framed as a quote rather than a checkout: the card reads "Customized solutions start at $229/month" and the button asks for a demo. A promotion was running when we re-read the page on 13 October 2026 — 50% off for three months with code FALL26, showing Lite at $39.50 and Core at $64.50 — and the footnote dates it: new customers only, ending 31 October. On 10 September the same FALL26 offer was dated to 30 September, and in August it ran as SUMMER26 to 31 August, so the deadline moves. What matters is still what you pay in month four. The trial is 15 days and takes no credit card. Lite and Core each include 2 users; Advanced includes 3. Aplos's help centre ('How to Manage Your Subscription', read 13 October 2026) adds what the plan cards leave out: all platform subscriptions include two users and further users cost $20 per month per user; the base subscription includes up to 500 contacts and the price rises $20 a month for each additional 1,000; and annual billing receives a 10% discount.

tools.name: Arbor
tools.price_note: Free for households, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17, on 2026-10-06 and again on 2026-10-09. Arbor has no pricing page at all — the URL 404s — and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture produced a figure. That is consistent with the model: Arbor is paid a referral fee by the winning electricity supplier, not by you. US-only: its own FAQ (read 6 October 2026) lists 12 states plus Washington DC (CT, DE, IL, MA, MD, ME, NH, NJ, NY, OH, PA and RI), and Texas is not on that list even though the site footer carries a Texas broker registration, so check your zip code before assuming coverage. It acts only on the supply portion of your bill. The delivery charges from your utility are untouched, so the saving applies to part of the bill rather than to all of it.

tools.name: Aspire
tools.entry_price_terms: a month (SGD)
tools.price_note: (price re-verified 2026-10-09 against the vendor's own pricing page, in a browser and by plain fetch) SGD $0 monthly fee on Basic, no minimum balance and no deposit to open. You pay per use: FX from 0.46% to send on Basic. That send rate has moved on this page: 0.46% on 11 September, 0.23% on 2 October and 0.46% again on 9 October 2026, so check the rate in your own account before a large conversion. The 9 October comparison table no longer shows the receive and instant-conversion rates or the SWIFT fees; our 2 October reading had from 0.34% to receive, from 0.22% for instant conversion, inbound SWIFT SGD $35 for SGD accounts or USD $8 for others, and outbound SWIFT USD $15 for SHA and USD $30 for OURS. Premium is SGD $15/month: 0% FX on the first SGD $13,000 of conversions a month, after which the Basic send rate applies, and 5 free outbound transfers worth up to USD $75 a month.

tools.name: Assembly
tools.entry_price_terms: a month, billed annually ($49 billed monthly)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 28 September 2026 in a rendered browser, both billing tabs and the full comparison table) Assembly, the client-portal platform at assembly.com, publishes five tiers. Free, a free-forever plan: $0 with 5 active contacts, 1 internal user, 50 build credits a month and 3 apps. Starter: $29 a month billed yearly or $49 monthly, 50 active contacts, 1 internal user. Professional: $99 billed yearly or $139 monthly, 500 active contacts, 3 internal users included and each extra one +$29 a month yearly or +$39 monthly. Advanced: $499 billed yearly or $599 monthly, unlimited active contacts, 5 internal users included and each extra one +$59 or +$79. Enterprise is quoted after a demo. Every paid plan includes 200 build credits a month and 5 apps; extra credits are $0.60 each up to 10,000 a month, unused credits roll over for one month, and extra apps are $5 a month each. If you bill clients through Assembly, cards cost 2.9% + $0.30 on every plan and ACH 1% (capped at $10 from Professional up); the table also lists store fees of 2.0%, 1.5%, 1% and 0.7% from Free to Advanced, invoices at +0.7% down to +0.3% and recurring subscriptions at +1.1% down to +0.5%. The FAQ says there are no setup, hosting or per-client fees, no contracts on self-serve plans, and downgrades take effect at the end of the billing period. Correction: until 28 September 2026 this field described a different company's employee-recognition plan at $3 per user; that was never the price of Assembly's client portal.

tools.name: BackupMaster
tools.entry_price_terms: Essentials · per month for a live store up to 300 orders a month
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/backup-master) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial. Agency is free to install but only for Shopify Partner development stores before they are transferred to a client, with all features enabled for three months. Essentials $19 a month or $205.20 a year, a 10% saving, covers stores up to 300 orders a month. That is automatic daily backups of products, collections, themes, blogs, pages, files, metafields, metaobjects, translations, customers, orders and inventories, restore of supported items, 365-day retention and unlimited cloud storage. Pro $39 a month or $421.20 a year covers up to 600 orders a month and adds downloadable backup copies, Google Drive sync and duplication of data for staging or expansion. Plus $79 a month or $853.20 a year covers up to 1,500 orders a month, and adds multi-store pricing, detailed audit logs, external portal access, a custom backup time and priority support. The listing says higher-volume plans exist on the vendor's own pricing page without printing what they cost. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer BackupMaster, Bondi, NSW, Australia; the app launched 4 August 2017, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, is available in English and German, and had 108 reviews at the time of writing. tools.name: Bybit
tools.price_note: No subscription — per-trade fees, re-verified 2026-10-16 against Bybit's own fee schedule, which still says it was last updated on 2 September 2026; the base VIP table below is unchanged since our 5 September reading. At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker; perpetuals and futures 0.0200% maker and 0.0550% taker; options 0.0200% maker and 0.0300% taker. The VIP ladder cuts those toward zero — at Supreme VIP spot is 0.0300% maker and 0.0450% taker, derivatives 0.0000% maker and 0.0300% taker, options 0.0050% and 0.0150%. Note that the top derivatives maker rate is zero rather than a rebate: we found no negative maker fee in the published table. That base table is not the only one, and the others start higher: fiat-crypto spot pairs cost 0.2000% taker and 0.1500% maker under $100,000 of 30-day volume, the Spot Adventure Zone and xStocks 0.2000% both ways at VIP 0, and Pre-Market Perpetuals and the Innovation Zone 0.0400% maker and 0.1000% taker — so a new account trading the newest listings pays about double the headline rate. Your VIP level is set by your asset balance, your 30-day average net borrowing or your trading volume over the past 30 days, whichever qualifies you higher, and it refreshes daily at 07:00 UTC. Bybit adds that actual rates can vary by region and points you to your own My Fee Rate page.

tools.name: CloudTask
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-08, read on their own pricing page and FAQ) Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. A one-time $299 deposit starts your search — asked “Do you charge a monthly platform fee?” their FAQ answers “No. There is a one-time $299 deposit to start your search. That is the only fee outside the models above.” — and the deposit applies toward your buyout or your first placement. Direct Hire costs 20% to 30% of first-year base salary, paid once and quoted per role, with a 6-month replacement guarantee (one replacement, same job description) and US W2 employment available. Managed Staffing is billed as one all-in monthly rate per person covering salary, compliance, payroll and support — that rate is not published, and it is the number that decides what this costs. It carries a 24-month replacement guarantee with replacements not capped, and time and activity tracking on by default, which the hire agrees to before matching and you can switch off when you post the role. For roles that create demand — outbound SDRs, BDRs, demand generation and full-cycle AEs — Managed Staffing runs on a six-month minimum term; Direct Hire has no minimum term. Converting a managed hire to direct employment is possible, but their FAQ makes it subject to a conversion fee and a notice period and publishes neither. Commissions and bonuses you add are separate from the all-in monthly rate. Health and equipment benefits are available on request on Managed Staffing only.

tools.name: Datarails
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-25 on www.datarails.com/pricing) There is no public price. Datarails publishes three plans — Professional, Premium and Expert — and every one of them carries a Request Quote button where the number would be. The page frames that as a feature: “Get a custom quote tailored to your needs. Complete cost transparency, with no consultant fees—ever.”

What the page does publish is the shape of the ladder, and it is unusually explicit about what changes between tiers. The comparison table lists the same feature set on all three plans: reporting, planning, dashboards, Data Mapper, Lookups, Workflows, Submit Button, File Boxes, Filters, version control, the Datarails AI Suite, the FinanceOS AI Connector and permissions. Only two rows differ. Professional gives 1 integration and 2 users with standard support. Premium, marked most popular, gives 2 integrations and 5 users with premium support, and adds AI Storyboards, described as board decks in one click. In August 2026 Expert gave 3 integrations and 15 users with premium support plus one “additional product included”. Re-read on 10 October 2026 the cards are more specific: Premium bundles Datarails Spend (cards, bill pay, contracts), and Expert bundles Cash Management, Month-End Close, Receivables and Desk, with 15 users plus 50 viewers and 3 integrations. The same page also calls Cash, Month-End Close, Spend and Desk modules “you can layer onto any plan”, without a price.

So the meter is seats and connected systems, not features. The page states no currency, no billing period, no minimum term and does not say whether a quote is annual, and there is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup: the only entry point on every page of the site is Request Demo or Request Quote. Treat any Datarails figure you have seen quoted elsewhere as unverified — on 25 August 2026 the vendor's own pricing page contains no amount at all.

One of those unpublished terms the vendor will answer if you ask. On 31 August 2026, through its partner team, Datarails told us that customers typically commit to an annual term, that billing can run monthly across that year, that users can be added as a team grows, and that adding modules or capabilities beyond the core platform can carry an extra cost that depends on the scope of the expansion. That is the vendor's own account rather than a published rate, so it belongs in your quote in writing — but it does answer the term question the pricing page leaves open.

tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-14 on flatpay.com/en-gb/pricing and their separate /pricelist page; the four transaction rates and up-front fees unchanged since 2026-08-13, the minimum monthly turnover changed -- see below) Flatpay charges one rate per transaction on every card type, with no monthly subscription. The card terminal is 1.49% and costs GBP 0 to start. The three point-of-sale tiers all run at 1.69% and differ only in what you pay up front for onboarding and installation: GBP 995 for mobile POS, GBP 1,495 for POS Pro and GBP 2,495 for POS Premium. Every one of those four prices is labelled "Below GBP 200,000 in annual card turnover". CHANGED SINCE AUGUST: the above-threshold panel is no longer reachable on the UK page -- there is no visible toggle, and the markup for it sits in a display:none component variant. That hidden markup holds both a "custom rate - contact sales" variant and a "0,99% / EUR 0" variant; neither renders for a UK visitor, and the comma decimal and euro sign mark the second as another market's card, so we do not quote 0.99% as a Flatpay UK rate (a WebFetch read it as a live figure on 2026-08-20 and that was wrong then too). tools.name: GCheck
tools.entry_price_terms: Basic · per background check, current county of residence only
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-16 on gcheck.com/pricing-packages after GCheck's partner mail announced a lower Basic price; first read 2026-09-29, including its FAQ) Three packages, each priced per background check, with no setup fees, no minimums and no long-term contracts. Basic is $18.95 per check (it was $19.95 when we first read the page on 29 September) and covers an SSN trace and address history, a national criminal database search, the nationwide sex offender registry, the OIG excluded parties list, OFAC sanctions lists, global watchlists and a county criminal search in the candidate's current county of residence only. Standard, marked Most Popular, is $39.95 per check and adds biometric identity verification and county criminal searches in every county on the candidate's full address history. Advanced, marked Recommended, is $49.95 per check and adds a federal criminal search across every federal district on that same address history. An asterisk on all three prices reads: additional third-party fees may apply to some products and are passed through with no markup; the page does not list those fees. Employers running more than 50 checks a year are pointed to a custom quote, which is where the page places ATS and HRIS integrations and customised workflows, and GCheck states that volume pricing and merit-based nonprofit discounts exist without publishing either. Everything else in the catalogue — drug tests (DOT, 5-panel and 10-panel), motor vehicle and CDL records, employment, education and reference verification, credit, bankruptcy, eviction, liens and judgments searches, fingerprinting, Form I-9 and E-Verify, and international searches — carries no public price. GCheck is based at 8335 W Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, and gives its phone number as 844-424-3254.

Team starts at the same $9.99/month ($6.99 discounted) for 5 computers and 5 users on 5 TB; Business starts at $19.99/month ($13.99 discounted) for 500 GB with unlimited users. Two further conditions sit in the same footnotes: going over your storage limit costs $0.25/GB/month on Personal and $0.50/GB/month on Team and Business, and the discount is for new signups only and is not available if you sign up from IDrive's mobile apps. tools.entry_price_terms: a month, or $30 a month billed annually ($350/yr)
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-10-03 on their own plans page, USD, tax excluded) Managed WordPress hosting from $35/mo for a single site, or $30/mo billed annually at $350 a year, with the first month free on top — Kinsta advertises annual as two months off. That entry plan carries one WordPress install, 10GB storage, 20GB server bandwidth, 125GB CDN bandwidth and 14 days of backup retention, and you choose whether it is metered on bandwidth or on visits, which is a real change from the visit-only plans older reviews describe. The multi-site ladder runs WP 2 at $70/mo or $59 billed annually ($700 a year), WP 5 at $115 or $96 ($1,150), WP 10 at $225 or $188 ($2,250), WP 20 at $340 or $284 ($3,400) and WP 40 at $450 or $375 ($4,500). Agency plans start at that same $340/mo, or $284 billed annually. Above them sits an Enterprise line our earlier readings missed entirely: it starts at $500/mo, or $417 billed annually, with $5,000 payable on signup. Several things that look like plan features are priced separately — dedicated servers from $300/mo, PHP performance at $10 per 500MB a month, external backups to AWS or Google Cloud at $2 per site a month plus $1 per GB, and more frequent backups at $20 a site for six-hourly or $100 for hourly. tools.name: TheTop
tools.price_note:
(read 19 September 2026) TheTop publishes no price. The navigation carries no pricing link, every button is Book a demo, and the page this review's figures came from is gone: thetop.com/pricing returns a hard 404, as do /pricing/ and /plans.

The $8 a month and $80 a year this review used to quote were withdrawn along with the product they belonged to, and cannot be bought today. Until September this was a personal assistant on a single tier, built around a morning brief from Gmail and a calendar. TheTop is now enterprise software sold through a sales call.

Read the figures on their site carefully, because it is full of dollar amounts that are not prices: the dashboard mock-ups show an AI invoice of $196,090, a month billed at $137,644 against a $176,920 baseline, and $39,276 saved. Those illustrate what the product reports, not what it costs. Nothing on the public site says what you would pay for TheTop itself.

What the site does commit to about commercial shape: deployment is single-tenant, one dedicated instance per customer; onboarding runs in three steps that start read-only (connect analytics, watch for about a month to establish your number, then point traffic at the Engine); and no traffic migration is needed on day one. Expect a contract quoted against your own AI spend rather than a list price — ask for the pricing basis in writing before the demo, because a layer that bills against measured savings and one that bills a flat platform fee are very different deals.

tools.price_note: (read 2026-10-13 in a live browser on xtiles.app/en/pricing, prices in US dollars, with the comparison table and FAQ) Four plans, priced per user. Free costs nothing and gives unlimited pages and projects, free templates, 3 personal spaces, Google and Outlook calendar, an AI assistant with 1,000 credits and limited AI integrations; the table adds file uploads of up to 5MB, two weeks of planner history (in our test on 21 October 2026: the current and the previous week) and one shared space. Plus is $19 a month, or $12.42 a month billed yearly, which the page says saves $79 a year: 100+ premium templates, recurring tasks, unlimited personal spaces, premium widgets, an unlimited AI assistant, basic AI integrations, full planner history, linked pages and unlimited file uploads. Pro is $35 a month, or $24.92 billed yearly (saving $121 a year): two 45-minute personal onboarding sessions, unlimited shared spaces and unlimited AI integrations, which let ChatGPT, Claude and other assistants connected to xTiles edit any project and work in shared workspaces; several AI permissions in the comparison table, among them editing structure and access rights, are marked soon. Enterprise is custom, with SAML SSO, a dedicated account manager and organisation spaces. VAT may apply. Educators, students and non-profits can get 50% off Plus for one year. The FAQ says subscriptions renew automatically, a monthly plan can be refunded in full within 72 hours and an annual one within 30 days, promotional and discounted plans are non-refundable, and only annual Plus can be upgraded to Pro with a calculated difference.

tools.name: Your Company Formations
tools.entry_price_terms: Digital · one-off, per formation, excluding 20% VAT
tools.price_note: (read 2026-10-18 in a browser on yourcompanyformations.co.uk/packages/compare-packages/, prices in pounds) One-off packages for forming a UK limited company, each plus the £100 Companies House incorporation fee, which is added separately. VAT at 20% applies to the package price and paid extras but not to the Companies House fee. Digital is £2.48: formation and official digital documents by email. Digital & Print is £6.98 and adds printed copies by post. Privacy is £17.48 and adds a London EC1 registered office address and a director's service address. Fully Inclusive is £44.48 and adds business mail forwarding, VAT registration and a Premium 12 Month Company Filing Service. Non-Resident is £98.48, with London address services, VAT registration, filing support and international document postage. Entrepreneurs is £315.00, with London address services, VAT and PAYE registration, filing support and 12 months of call answering. Identity verification for Companies House (ACSP service) is included for up to four officers. Every basket starts with a £5.99 pre-submission review that you can remove at checkout. The yearly services renew at a price: the registered office address £29 a year plus VAT, the director's service address £28, business mail forwarding £98, and the Premium filing service £128 a year excluding VAT, with the £50 Companies House confirmation statement fee paid separately. Other company types, such as limited by guarantee, charity, property management, right to manage, LLP and PLC, have their own packages.

tools.name: Zedonk
tools.entry_price_terms: per month, billed annually
tools.price_note: (price re-verified 2026-09-09, re-read unchanged 2026-09-27 and again 2026-10-20 against zedonk.co.uk/pricing; unchanged since our August reading) Modular fashion-ERP, priced per building block and billed annually, all listed as 'prices starting from': PLM £166/mo, ERP Essential £166/mo, B2C £250/mo and B2B £332/mo. The two upper cards read 'All ERP Essential Features PLUS' — Shopify integration and barcode generation on B2C, the B2B digital showroom on B2B — so those tiers contain the ERP rather than sitting on top of it. No self-serve signup: every tier goes through a demo, and the FAQ states the displayed plans are 'merely examples' and that a plan can be changed at any time. Onboarding and training are included in every plan; the FAQ puts implementation cost (customisation, data migration, integrations) in a separate figure quoted in a consultation. The general FAQ puts the floor as 'from as little as £1990 per year', which is the £166 card times twelve, rounded.

flags.evidence: The 'starting from' wording is doing real work: £166/mo is the floor of the cheapest module, billed annually, so a working setup for a brand that sells wholesale quickly stacks toward £332/mo and beyond — about £4,000 a year before add-ons.

tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-09-22 on zenbusiness.com/pricing-products/, where /pricing/ now redirects; every one of the sixteen published amounts unchanged since 25 Jul 2026) Formation itself is $0 plus the state's fee — that applies to LLC, S corp and C corp filings alike, and the state fee is separate, varies by state and is not shown until you pick one. Everything else is priced as its own line rather than bundled into plan tiers. The recurring items are registered agent at $199/year, Worry-Free Compliance Filing at $199/year, and Advanced Compliance Protection at $299/year. One-time filings: operating agreement $99, EIN $99, business document templates $99, rush filing $79 and DBA registration $95 plus state fees. Then business licence report $149, amendment $100, certificate of good standing $100, annual report filing $100 per report, and New York publication $200 for the state that requires it. There is a second catalogue alongside the legal one: business website $129/year, eCommerce website $279/year, business email address $25/year, domain $25/year, domain privacy $10/year, logo kit $60, business banking $5/month and Money Pro with online payments $30/month.

tools.name: Zenind
tools.price_note: (read 2026-10-07 on zenind.com/pricing in a browser render, USD) Three US company formation packages, each a one-time fee plus state filing fees, which the page showed as $120.00 as it loaded and which change with the state you choose. Basic is $0.00: name availability check, preparation and filing of the state documents, filing within 7 days, lifetime customer support and an online company dashboard. Standard is $149.00: filing in 3 days, plus EIN application preparation, BOI report preparation, membership or stock certificates, a prepared operating agreement or bylaws, and meeting minutes. Premium is $249.00: filing in 1 business day, plus the compliance and annual report service (first year included, then $100 a year) and a dedicated account manager. Every package says an additional $99 a year applies if you use Zenind's registered address and registered agent service. Separately priced: registered agent $99 a year in all 50 states and DC, operating agreement or bylaws $99 one-time on Basic, an extra BOI report $29, certificate of good standing $99 plus government fees, federal trademark registration $199 plus USPTO fees, sales and use tax registration $299 plus government fees, and online notary $25 plus $10 per extra seal.
